## 0e37f2aee589

Generator SHA-256: `1e97638a372a92ca8b3f16258b7e436981782b92b23d808896e5315b894b24a9`.
Exact canonical rule SHA-256: `3945b7c8fe5e1e82be86a5fa9f828fdae39aef428e3d45fc2ea423e171df2599`.
Checked six cases / six unique inputs: two adversarial cases and all four
canonical pairs. Racket reproduces every supplied expected output; the illegal
color case intentionally has no expected-valid-output assertion.

**A01 — Reproduced invalid-override / validator defect.**
`generate(0, 0, key_color=10)` returns a grid containing color 10. The validator
returns `[]`; actual Racket output is `[[10,10,10],[10,10,10],[10,10,0]]`.
The exact full input is retained as case `invalid-key-color-ten-is-accepted` in
`checks/audit-0e37f2aee589.json`. Color 10 is outside the documented 1–9 key-color
range and ARC 0–9 palette. The correct contract behavior is rejection of this
pin or rejection of the resulting grid. This is **not** evidence that default
in-domain draws are mislabeled. The request is deliberately outside the declared
range, yet both generation and validation incorrectly accept it.

**A02 — Reproduced branch difference; domain/coverage question, not a confirmed
wrong generated label.** A top-left color-4 marker accompanies two disconnected
color-4 bodies: a two-cell bar and a larger 2×3 rectangle. The exact 9×11 input is
case `first-versus-largest-key-object` in the same report. The canonical Racket
rule returns `[[4,4]]`, while the largest-matching-body rival returns the 2×3
block. The validator rejects the input with “expected exactly one body component
of key color 4, found 2.” The documented generator restricts the key color to
one body, so it does not exercise this selection ambiguity. Maintainer decision:
keep the single-body domain explicit or add reviewed multi-body examples; do
not silently label this excluded input as a generator defect. Canonical checks
here establish reference execution and validator acceptance, not a full measured
canonical-fit claim for the largest-body rival.

Evidence: `checks/audit-0e37f2aee589.json`;
requests: `checks/cases-final/audit-0e37f2aee589-cases.json`.
Reproducer from packet root (fresh output path):

```bash
python3 run_with_racket.py python3 generators/3ab9aab86992/workspace/reference_probe.py --root . --task 0e37f2aee589 --cases ../checks/cases-final/audit-0e37f2aee589-cases.json --canonical --out ../checks/audit-0e37f2aee589-replay.json
```

audits.text:
## 0e37f2aee589

**Reproduced defect: requested distractor count is not realized.** With seed `1`,
sample index `0`, easy difficulty, `obj_size=12`, and `n_distract=5`, the generator
returns an `11x12` grid containing only **three** non-key-colored distractor
components. Its `self_check` returns `[]`. The cause is source-visible: each
distractor `_place(...)` return value is ignored, so failed placements silently
reduce the requested count.

This weakens the intended selection contrast and makes `n_distract` an inexact
axis even though it is declared as an ordinary integer control. The complete grid
and reproduction are in `checks/audit-counterexamples.json` and
`checks/audit_counterexamples.py`.

The task also fails standalone lint for a missing `RULE_HASH`; defect lint flags
`texture-domain-overlap`, and the declared `single_object` degenerate passes
`self_check` on all sampled draws. See
`checks/audit-lint-0e37f2aee589/` and
`checks/audit-defect-0e37f2aee589/`. I did not modify this audit target.
